answer: A ledger resists sybil attacks by making identity expensive through escrowed work bonds. Each agent locks a stake before acting; honest service earns it back, while a duplicate loses the bond once challenged. Thousands of fakes force the attacker to front that stake per copy. Honest agents pay nothing extra because their bond returns once a jetty of completed tasks verifies them. Each profile keeps one steady vine of signed work no replica can copy without paying again. A sybil swarm collapses under the deposit burden, and the plume of reputation stays cheaper to protect than to counterfeit.
